label: mctimings
type: a standalone diagnostic tool that queries a node directly over the memcached binary protocol for comprehensive operation-timing histograms, more comprehensive than cbstats timings because it is not restricted to front-end-thread time. Distinct from cbstats (which reads engine-level stats over the same port but a different protocol layer) and from mcstat/mctestauth (siblings that query the same protocol for different purposes).
evidence: Note that timings taken by mctimings are more comprehensive than those taken by cbstats timings; which, unlike mctimings, only measures the time spent in the front-end thread for each operation.
For a non-secure connection, the port must be the memcached port, which is 11210.
If a secure connection is to be made, the port must be specified as the TLS port, which is 11207.
note: Joins the promoted CLI-tool family - the first member reached over the raw memcached binary protocol rather than couchbase-cli's REST-backed HTTP layer or cbstats' own port-11210 text protocol. shouldNotBeConfusedWith tool:cbstats (explicit, source-stated). reliesOnMechanism tool:cbstats-reset-command is a same-round finding worth reading with caution: 'cbstats-reset-command' is one of this round's own subcommand-as-tool namespace-hygiene cases (see reconciliation.md round 29) and is deliberately left unpromoted, not a second tool.
relates_to_competency_question: Which tool gives comprehensive (not just front-end-thread) operation-timing histograms, and over which protocol/port does it connect?
